2026-10-14.meal: Reheat: Sunday's sweet potato & spinach dhal with rice
2026-10-14.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15-7:45pm (The Lindum) — quick reheat gets tea done either side of the run

steps: Tip the dhal into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8-10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4-5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the dhal heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot before serving.

2026-10-15.meal: Garlic butter baked haddock with crushed new potatoes & peas
2026-10-15.note: Normal evening, nothing on for tea

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15-18 minutes until tender.
Mix the melted butter with the garlic and a squeeze of lemon. Put the haddock on a lined tray and brush over the butter.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily.
Cook the peas for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain and lightly crush the potatoes with a fork, stir through the parsley and a knob of butter.
Serve the fish with the crushed potatoes, peas and lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: leave the garlic butter off her portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-10-16.note: Free evening — gymnastics 9:30am & swimming 1:30pm today, but nothing on for tea

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan). Boil the new potatoes for 15 minutes until tender.
Put the salmon skin-side down on a lined tray. Drizzle with the oil, squeeze over half the lemon and season.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, until it flakes easily.
Steam or boil the green beans for the last 4 minutes of the potatoes.
Drain the potatoes and toss with the butter. Serve with lemon wedges.
recipe.tip: Air fryer instead: 180°C for 10–12 minutes. Flake Mathilda's portion and check carefully for bones.

2026-10-17.note: Francis's away match at Chapeltown (KO 14:30) means a long round trip — slow cooker on before we leave so tea's ready when we're back

ingredients: Grated cheese & soured cream, to serve (optional)
steps: Soften the onion and pepper in the oil in a frying pan for 5 minutes (or skip this and put everything straight into the slow cooker if you're short on time).
Add the garlic, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute.
Tip the onion mixture, beans, chopped tomatoes and tomato purée into the slow cooker. Stir well and season.
Cover and cook on low for 6–7 hours (or high for 3–4), until thick and the veg is tender.
Take out Mathilda's portion, then stir the chilli flakes through the rest.
Cook the rice for 15 minutes before serving. Serve the chilli over rice with cheese and soured cream if using.
recipe.tip: Slow cooker on by 9am before we set off for Chapeltown. Mathilda: take hers out before the chilli flakes go in and keep it mild.

2026-10-18.note: This week's one meat night. Hull fixture time still TBC — the slow cooker keeps tea ready whenever we're back, and the extra goes in the freezer for the meal drawer

ingredients: 1 beef stock cube, dissolved in 200ml hot water
Parmesan or vegetarian hard cheese, to serve
steps: Brown the mince in batches in a frying pan, then drain off any excess fat and tip into the slow cooker.
Soften the onion, carrots and celery in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute. Add to the slow cooker.
Stir in the chopped tomatoes, tomato purée, stock and herbs. Season.
Cover and cook on low for 6–7 hours (or high for 3–4), stirring once if you're around.
Take out Mathilda's portion, then cool the extra portions you're freezing before serving the rest.
Cook the spaghetti for 10 minutes and serve with the sauce and parmesan.
recipe.tip: Cool the extra fully within an hour, then portion, label and freeze for the meal drawer — no raw dump bags. Mathilda: mash hers a little finer.

2026-10-19.meal: Veggie chickpea & spinach curry with rice
2026-10-19.note: Free evening — good day to batch-cook extra for Tuesday's busy night after Hull hockey training

steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder and cumin and cook for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas, chopped tomatoes and stock. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Take out Mathilda's portion and 4 portions to cool for Tuesday before seasoning the rest.
Stir the spinach into the remainder and cook for 3–4 minutes until wilted.
Cook the rice and serve with the curry.
Cool Tuesday's 4 portions within an hour, cover and keep in the fridge.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep hers mild — no curry powder in her portion, just the chickpeas and veg.

2026-10-20.meal: Reheat: Monday's chickpea & spinach curry with rice
2026-10-20.note: Hull Hockey Training 6–7pm (Hymers College) plus travel — tea ready for whoever's not driving, kept warm for the rest

ingredients: 4 portions Monday's chickpea & spinach curry (from the fridge)
steps: Tip the curry into a pan with a splash of water.
Heat gently, stirring, until bubbling and piping hot all the way through (about 8–10 minutes). Or microwave in a covered bowl for 4–5 minutes, stirring halfway.
Cook the rice while the curry heats.
Serve straightaway.
recipe.tip: Only reheat it once, and check it's piping hot all the way through before serving. Anyone back late from training can have their portion microwaved separately.

2026-10-21.note: Hockey Academy Night 6:15–7:45pm (The Lindum) — air fryer gets tea done fast either side of the run

ingredients: 4 servings mash (fresh potatoes, or microwave pouches for speed)
Butter & milk, for the mash (if making fresh)
steps: Air fry the fishcakes at 190°C for 12–15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and piping hot all the way through (check the pack for exact timing).
If making fresh mash, boil chunked potatoes for 15 minutes, drain, then mash with butter and a splash of milk.
Cook the peas in a pan of boiling water for 4–5 minutes, or microwave.
Drain and serve everything together.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: cut hers into pieces and check it's piping hot through the middle before serving. Microwave mash pouches work well on a short turnaround.

2026-10-22.note: Free evening, nothing on for tea

steps: Cook the pasta according to the pack instructions, then drain and run under cold water to cool slightly.
Cook the sweetcorn for 3–4 minutes if frozen, or just drain if tinned.
Mix the tuna, mayonnaise and lemon juice in a big bowl.
Stir in the pasta, sweetcorn and red pepper. Season.
Serve with salad leaves on the side.
recipe.tip: Mathilda: keep her tuna mayo light, and swap the raw pepper for cucumber sticks on the side if she's not keen.
